private_note: My household is top fifth under every plan, so I simply rank by the top-fifth number: Cedar 318, Today 252, Alder 242, Hazel 159, Birch 144. Cedar is a 26% gain; Hazel and Birch would cut us by over a third, so failure beats them. Alder costs little, so if Cedar can't reach nine, I'd rather a deadlock than Alder, though barely. Watch the straw poll before conceding anything.
statement: I'll be direct: I'm a surgeon, my spouse is a lawyer, and we're in the top fifth whatever happens here. I back Cedar. Look at the numbers rather than the labels. Cedar is the only plan that grows the economy: average income rises from 100 to 115. The middle, fourth and top fifths all come out ahead, so that's three of five groups, a clear majority of households. Hazel and Birch shrink average income by a fifth, and they cut the middle and fourth fifths too, not just people like me. I know Cedar asks real sacrifice of the lowest two groups, and I won't pretend otherwise. But a convention that shrinks the whole pie for a generation is a hard thing to justify. Remember that failure leaves us with today's arrangements, which I can live with. I'm open to hearing what each of you needs.
